summary: Maleo Airport (MOH) is a small regional airport serving Morowali Regency in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. It primarily supports the Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP), one of the world's largest nickel processing and stainless steel production complexes. The airport plays a vital role in connecting the remote mining and industrial hub to major Indonesian cities despite its modest infrastructure.
faqs:
Q: What is Maleo Airport primarily used for?
A: The airport mainly serves business travelers and workers associated with the Morowali Industrial Park, along with local residents of the regency.

Q: Which airlines operate at Maleo Airport?
A: Several Indonesian carriers typically serve the airport, including flights connecting to Makassar and other major cities, though schedules can be limited.

Q: How large is Maleo Airport?
A: It is classified as a small airport with basic facilities, featuring a single runway and a modest terminal building.

Q: Is the airport open to international flights?
A: No, Maleo Airport handles domestic flights only and does not have international customs or immigration facilities.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options are limited, so arranging a hotel pickup or pre-booked vehicle in advance is strongly recommended. Taxi services may be available at the terminal but are not always reliable due to the small volume of traffic. Allow extra time for travel between the airport and the industrial park or town center, as road conditions can vary.
local_tip: Bring cash in small Indonesian rupiah denominations, as local vendors and transport providers in Morowali often lack card payment facilities, and ATMs can be unreliable outside the main town.
